g.id: Typical cover depth: 1.92 m built, 1.75 m here
Typical gradient: 4.98 mm/m built, 5.00 mm/m here
Nine in ten below: 4.58 m built, 5.02 m here
This was the check that mattered. The minimum-gradient and cover rules behave the way a real designer's did
616 dead ends over 84 km, against 334 over 79 km built
The design used to sprout a branch down every street
560 short dead-end branches dropped - those houses join the street they came off
Junctions per km: 3.9 built, 6.5 before, 3.6 NOW
Typical run: 65 m built, 48 m before, 105 m NOW - fewer, longer trenches
Obvious reading: tighter spacing lets the pipe follow the ground and stay shallow
Their manholes sit 30 m apart, ours 43 m
TESTED at five spacings, 100 m down to 30 m
FALSE. Chambers nearly double, 1,870 to 3,602, and depth does not improve at all
So we do NOT copy it. Fewest manholes stands
Their network almost never runs along a dual carriageway - 4 pipes in 3,267
That confirms the rule, and made our chambers sitting on one a real fault. 34 down to 5
ONE DIFFERENCE TO KEEP IN MIND

g.text: ONE DIFFERENCE TO KEEP IN MIND

g.id: Not because it is cleverer: because it PUMPS
Their network digs past 6 m far less often than ours - 1.4 percent against 6.1
30.8 km of rising main against 188.6 km of gravity - about one metre in seven
W7 pumps NOTHING, because the main pipe alignment you drew gives every part of town a short route
They bought shallow trenches with pumping stations. W7 gets them from the alignment
W7 CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK NAMA ALREADY BUILT - 188.6 km of gravity sewer, read from the KMZ files
